chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Suwayd al-Qalla' from Ayub from Hariz from Burayd al-Ajli from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who deposited wealth with me, then he died, and he had no children, and he had not performed the Hajj of Islam. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Perform Hajj on his behalf, and give him whatever remains.'
And there is no harm if a man takes payment for a Hajj and gives it to someone else. Narrated.

key_terms.اِسْتَوْدَعَنِي: Deposited with me / entrusted to me
key_terms.حَجَّةً: A performance of Hajj (as a unit of service)
key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: The first obligatory Hajj performed by a Muslim

ai.seo_question: What happens to the wealth of a deceased person who missed Hajj and had no heirs, according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *Hajj al-Bada'il* (substitute Hajj) funded by deposited wealth (*Wadi'ah*) when the depositor dies without heirs, prioritizing the fulfillment of the missed obligatory duty over inheritance claims. It further clarifies the permissibility of a *fee* for the agent performing the Hajj, distinguishing between the cost of the ritual and compensation for service, a nuance significant in Shia fiqh regarding *Hajj al-Muta'ah*.
